heard: a $264 million NASA spacecraft smashed into the desert. In 2001, Genesis launched to collect samples from 93 million miles away. It spent three years orbiting the sun to catch microscopic solar wind particles. This was the first mission since Apollo to return physical samples from deep space. But on September 8, 2004, the capsule hit the Utah sand at 193 miles per hour. The crash happened because four tiny gravity switches were installed upside down. They followed a flawed blueprint that prevented them from ever triggering the parachutes. Scientists still salvage the mission, proving the sun's chemistry is unique. That happened even though a $264 million NASA spacecraft smashed into the desert.
